intro_en: In this lesson you will learn to make the ない-form of verbs (the plain negative form). With it you can use three important sentence patterns: "please don't do" (〜ないでください), "must do" (〜なければなりません) and "don't have to do" (〜なくてもいいです). You will use them in everyday situations such as the hospital, health, and deadlines (までに).

g17-1.explanation_en: The ない-form is the plain (casual) negative form of a verb; in meaning it equals ません (書きません = 書かない = எழுதவில்லை / எழுத மாட்டேன், don't write / won't write). You use it as the base for all three patterns in this lesson (〜ないでください、〜なければなりません、〜なくてもいいです). Group I (う-verbs): change the last い-row sound of the ます-stem to the あ-row and add ない (書きます → 書か → 書かない、飲みます → 飲まない). But if the stem ends in い and the dictionary form ends in う (買います、吸います), it becomes わ, not あ: 買わない、吸わない. Group II (る-verbs): drop ます and add ない (食べます → 食べない、起きます → 起きない). Group III: します → しない、来ます → 来ない (こない). Only あります becomes just ない (×あらない). Just as the Tamil negative participle ending "-ஆத" in "சாப்பிடாத / போகாத" (not eating / not going) can describe things, the Japanese ない-form behaves like an い-adjective.
g17-1.tamil_parallel_en: Like the Tamil negative forms "-வில்லை" / "-ஆத": எழுதுகிறேன் → எழுதவில்லை / எழுதாத ("I write" → "didn't write / not writing") = 書きます → 書かない ; சாப்பிடுகிறேன் → சாப்பிடாத ("I eat" → "not eating") = 食べます → 食べない.
g17-1.formation_en: Group I: い-row → あ-row + ない: 書きます→書かない、聞きます→聞かない、飲みます→飲まない、読みます→読まない、休みます→休まない、返します→返さない、出します→出さない、待ちます→待たない、持ちます→持たない、帰ります→帰らない、入ります→入らない、乗ります→乗らない、脱ぎます→脱がない ; い-stem + う: 買います→買わない、吸います→吸わない、習います→習わない、使います→使わない / Group II: ます → ない: 食べます→食べない、見ます→見ない、起きます→起きない、寝ます→寝ない、忘れます→忘れない、覚えます→覚えない、入れます→入れない、浴びます→浴びない、降ります→降りない / Group III: します→しない、勉強します→勉強しない、来ます→来ない(こない) / Special: あります→ない
g17-1.pitfalls_en: Don't say ×買あない for 買います; it is ○買わない. The ない-form of 来ます is not ×きない but ○こない (the sound changes). あります → not ×あらない but ○ない.

g17-2.explanation_en: To politely tell someone not to do something ("please don't ..."), add でください to the ない-form. It is the negative of 〜てください (please do), which you learned in Lesson 14. It is just like adding "-ஆதீர்கள்" in Tamil: "புகை பிடிக்காதீர்கள்" (don't smoke), "மறக்காதீர்கள்" (don't forget). To give a reason, you can put 〜ですから / 〜ますから in front (危ないですから、入らないでください). With close friends you can drop ください and just say 〜ないで, but at N5 we use the full form.
g17-2.tamil_parallel_en: Like the Tamil polite negative command "-ஆதீர்கள்": புகை பிடிக்காதீர்கள் ("please don't smoke") = たばこを吸わないでください ; மறக்காதீர்கள் ("please don't forget") = 忘れないでください.
g17-2.formation_en: V ない-form + でください (吸わない + でください → 吸わないでください ; 忘れない + でください → 忘れないでください)
g17-2.pitfalls_en: It is not ×吸わなくてください but ○吸わないでください (ないで + ください). Also don't add ない to the て-form as in ×吸ってない.

g17-3.explanation_en: To express a duty, "must do", drop the final い of the ない-form and add ければなりません (飲まない → 飲まなければなりません). The literal meaning is "if you don't do it, it won't do", just like Tamil "சாப்பிடாவிட்டால் முடியாது" (it won't do if you don't eat) = "சாப்பிட்டே ஆக வேண்டும்" (you must eat). It is a long form, but memorise it as one chunk. Question: 〜なければなりませんか. If the answer is "yes", say はい、〜なければなりません; if "no need", say いいえ、〜なくてもいいです (the next grammar point). It often comes with 〜までに (g17-6) to give a deadline.
g17-3.tamil_parallel_en: Like Tamil "-ஏ ஆக வேண்டும்" (literally "it won't do if you don't"): மருந்து சாப்பிட்டே ஆக வேண்டும் ("you must take the medicine") = 薬を飲まなければなりません.
g17-3.formation_en: V ない-form (drop い) + ければなりません: 飲まない→飲まなければなりません、出さない→出さなければなりません、食べない→食べなければなりません、しない→しなければなりません、来ない→来なければなりません
g17-3.pitfalls_en: Although it looks like a negative, it means "must do", not "must not do". It is not ×飲まないければ; drop the い of ない to get ○飲まなければ.

g17-4.explanation_en: To say "it's fine even if you don't" = "you don't have to", drop the い of the ない-form and add くてもいいです (行かない → 行かなくてもいいです). It is the negative partner of 〜てもいいです (you may), from Lesson 15: instead of the て-form, you use なくて from the ない-form. Because ない behaves like an い-adjective, ない → なくて, just like 寒い → 寒くて. It matches Tamil "போகாவிட்டாலும் பரவாயில்லை" (it's fine even if you don't go) / "போக வேண்டாம்" (no need to go). Use it to answer "no" to a 〜なければなりませんか question.
g17-4.tamil_parallel_en: Like Tamil "-ஆவிட்டாலும் பரவாயில்லை": போகாவிட்டாலும் பரவாயில்லை ("it's fine even if you don't go" = "you don't have to go") = 行かなくてもいいです.
g17-4.formation_en: V ない-form (drop い) + くてもいいです: 行かない→行かなくてもいいです、飲まない→飲まなくてもいいです、来ない→来なくてもいいです、しない→しなくてもいいです
g17-4.pitfalls_en: It is not ×行かないでもいいです but ○行かなくてもいいです. Watch the difference: 〜てもいいです (you may do it) gives permission, while 〜なくてもいいです (you may skip it) gives an exemption.

g17-5.explanation_en: You can take an object that is normally marked with を, move it to the start of the sentence, and make it the topic with は: 薬を飲んでください → 薬は飲んでください. Then it means "as for the medicine, ...", just as in Tamil you can put the object first: "மருந்து, சாப்பாட்டுக்குப் பிறகு சாப்பிடுங்கள்" (the medicine, take it after meals). There are two uses: (1) continuing to talk about something already being discussed, and (2) contrasting: お酒は飲みますが、たばこは吸いません (I drink alcohol, but I don't smoke). When は comes in, を disappears; the two never appear together as ×薬をは.
g17-5.tamil_parallel_en: Like putting the object first as a topic in Tamil: மருந்து(ஐப் பற்றிச் சொன்னால்), சாப்பாட்டுக்குப் பிறகு சாப்பிடுங்கள் ("as for the medicine, take it after meals") = 薬はご飯のあとで飲んでください.
g17-5.formation_en: N(object) + は + … + V (は instead of を ; を disappears)
g17-5.pitfalls_en: ×薬をは → ○薬は. In a contrast sentence "X は… が、Y は…", both objects take は; this is an exception to the "one は per sentence" rule.

g17-6.explanation_en: までに = "by ...": a deadline meaning an action must happen once and be finished before (or at) that time. まで = "until ..." (Lesson 4): an action or state continues up to that time. 五時まで働きます (I work continuously until five) vs 五時までに帰ります (I go home once, by five). This is easy for you because Tamil has exactly the same difference between "-வரை" (until) and "-க்குள்" (by / within). Questions: いつまでに / 何時までに. It usually comes with 〜なければなりません or 〜てください.
g17-6.tamil_parallel_en: Tamil has the same split: "-க்குள்" = までに and "-வரை" = まで. ஐந்து மணிக்குள் திரும்புவேன் ("I'll be back by five") = 五時までに帰ります ; ஐந்து மணி வரை வேலை செய்வேன் ("I'll work until five") = 五時まで働きます.
g17-6.formation_en: N(time / day) + までに + V (an action that happens once) ; compare: N + まで + V (a continuing action)
g17-6.pitfalls_en: For "please come back by five", it is not ×五時まで帰ってください but ○五時までに. Use まで for continuing actions (働きます、待ちます、います) and までに for actions that finish once (帰ります、出します、返します).

items.L17-q01: 薬 = くすり (மருந்து, medicine). Don't voice it and read ぐすり; there is no word くつり.
items.L17-q02: 病気 = びょうき (நோய், illness). びょう is a long sound, so don't shorten it to びよき; and don't forget the voicing mark on び (it is not ひょうき).
items.L17-q03: 忘れる = わすれる (மறக்க, to forget); it is a Group II verb, so its ない-form is 忘れない (わすれない). わすらない is a wrong form made as if it were Group I.
items.L17-q04: からだ = 体 (உடல், body). 休 (やすみ) and 本 (ほん) are look-alike kanji; 体 is 人 + 本.
items.L17-q05: "To give back" (திருப்பிக் கொடுக்க) = 返す. 帰る (かえる = to go home, வீடு திரும்ப) is a different verb with the same sound; for a book it is 返す. 反 is only one part of 返.
items.L17-q06: "I have a headache" (தலை வலிக்கிறது) = 頭が痛い. 危ない (ஆபத்தான, dangerous) is not used for body pain.
items.L17-q07: To hand in homework (வீட்டுப்பாடத்தைச் சமர்ப்பிக்க) = 宿題を出す. 脱ぐ (கழற்ற, to take off) and 浴びる (குளிக்க, to shower) don't fit.
items.L17-q08: Having no money, "I'm in trouble" (சிரமப்படுகிறேன்) = 困っています. 忘れています (I've forgotten) doesn't fit the reason.
items.L17-q09: "To take a day off work" (அலுவலகத்துக்கு விடுப்பு எடுக்க) = 会社を休みます. 出します means "to take out / hand in", which doesn't fit with a place.
items.L17-q10: When politely offering something, say "N は いかがですか" (how about ...?). いくら (how much does it cost) and いくつ (how many) are different questions.
items.L17-q11: シャワーを浴びる = to take a shower (ஷவரில் குளிக்க). 入る is used as お風呂に入る (with に); with シャワーを, the verb is 浴びる.
items.L17-q12: "You don't have to go" = school is closed (பள்ளிக்கு விடுமுறை). 行かなければなりません (you must go) is the opposite meaning; 行かないでください is a prohibition.
items.L17-q13: 病気 (நோய், ill) = 体が悪い (உடல்நிலை சரியில்லை, in poor health). 体が強い means a strong body, the opposite meaning.
items.L17-q14: なければなりません = you must do it; the closest is 飲んでください. 飲まないでください (don't take it) is the opposite meaning; don't get confused just because you see ない.
items.L17-q15: 吸います has an い-stem, so its ない-form is 吸わない; then add でください. 吸いないで has the wrong stem; 吸わなくて is only for 〜なくてもいいです.
items.L17-q16: "Must" = ない-form minus い + ければなりません: 出さなければなりません. It is なりません, not ありません.
items.L17-q17: "You don't have to take it" (சாப்பிடாமல் இருக்கலாம்) = ない → なくて + もいいです: 飲まなくてもいいです. 飲まないでもいい is wrong; 飲みなくて has the wrong stem.
items.L17-q18: The deadline "by five o'clock" (ஐந்து மணிக்குள்) = までに. まで means "until five" (ஐந்து மணி வரை) and is for continuing actions; 帰る is an action that happens once.
items.L17-q19: In a contrast sentence "X は 〜が、Y は 〜", the second object also takes は. を is grammatically possible too, but when contrasting with が, は is the natural choice.
items.L17-q20: 来ます → 来ない (こない) → 来なくてもいいです. 来ないでもいい is wrong; 来なければ goes only with なりません.
items.L17-q21: The answer is いいえ、働かなくてもいいです (no need), so the question is "do I have to work?" (வேலை செய்தே ஆக வேண்டுமா?) = 働かなければなりませんか. 働かません is a wrong form (it should be 働きません).
items.L17-q22: 金曜日までに 本を 返さなければなりません。 The deadline (までに) comes first, then the object + を, and なければなりません at the end.
items.L17-q23: 危ないですから、ここに 入らないでください。 入る marks the place you go into with に; then the ない-form + でください.
items.L17-q24: 薬は ご飯の あとで 飲まなければなりません。 The object 薬 becomes the topic with は and goes first; "N の あとで" comes before the verb.
items.L17-q25: [1] The doctor advises you to take the medicine: 飲んでください. [2] When you have a cold, "don't take a bath" (குளிக்காதீர்கள்) = 入らないでください. [3] Since tomorrow is a day off, you must do the work by Friday: しなければなりません.
